claim: Fix a species richness \(k\ge3\), let \(n_1,\ldots,n_k\) be strictly positive integer abundances with total \(N\), and put \(r=N-k\). Compare Hill diversity of order \(1\), \({}^1D=\exp(H)\) with \(H=-\sum_i p_i\log p_i\), against Hill diversity of order \(\infty\), \({}^{\infty}D=1/\max_i p_i\), the reciprocal Berger–Parker dominance. For every fixed \(k\ge3\), the two indices induce the same weak ordering whenever \(r\le3\). At \(r=4\), weak-order agreement first fails only because Berger–Parker ties \((1^{k-2},3,3)\) with \((1^{k-3},2,2,3)\), while Shannon ranks the latter as more diverse. No opposite strict ranking occurs for \(r\le5\). At \(r=6\), strict reversal appears for the first time. For \(k=3\) the unique reversing pair is \((1,4,4)\) versus \((2,2,5)\). For every \(k\ge4\), the complete first strict layer consists of exactly two pairs: \((1^{k-2},4,4)\) versus \((1^{k-3},2,2,5)\), and \((1^{k-3},3,3,3)\) versus \((1^{k-4},2,2,2,4)\). In each pair the first profile has the smaller maximum abundance and hence larger order-\(\infty\) diversity, but also the larger Shannon product \(Q=\prod_i n_i^{n_i}\) and hence smaller order-\(1\) diversity. The all-\(k\) cutoff is exhaustive because after subtracting the mandatory one individual per species, profiles are partitions of \(r\); once \(k\ge r\), increasing richness only pads profiles with baseline ones and cannot change either comparison.
integrity: At fixed total, order-\(1\) diversity is ordered oppositely to the exact integer \(Q=\prod_i n_i^{n_i}\), while order-\(\infty\) diversity is ordered oppositely to \(\max_i n_i\). The verifier enumerates all relevant excess partitions, independently reconstructs abundance profiles, and checks the stabilization argument that extends the finite census to every richness.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns unlabeled strictly positive integer abundance profiles at common species richness and common total census size. The excess-six threshold is a discrete-resolution statement and does not provide an absolute threshold for arbitrary real relative-abundance vectors.
title: Six excess individuals are the sharp Shannon–Berger–Parker strict-ranking boundary
